implementation_summary: With no OS keychain, KeyResolver writes .qa-keys.json as one AES-256-GCM record: a new random 12-byte IV on every write, a required 16-byte tag, and the header authenticated. Writes go to a temp file (mode 600) and are renamed into place; saves in one process are queued. The encryption key is a random 256-bit key created once in the user's config folder (XDG_CONFIG_HOME, APPDATA or ~/.config, then qa-flow-tester/key-file.key), or derived with scrypt from QA_KEYS_ENCRYPTION_KEY when set. A legacy plaintext file is read once and rewritten encrypted. If encryption fails, saving throws; nothing is written in plain text. New saveServiceKey and resolveServiceKey handle the named service key 'pagespeed' (keychain account service:pagespeed, encrypted file, PAGESPEED_API_KEY). The keychain path is unchanged. ADR 0034 records the design and amends ADR 0002.

risks: Hosted beta: SessionKeyResolver in packages/runner/src/beta.ts does not override saveServiceKey or resolveServiceKey; called without a session, a service key would go to the shared encrypted file. Must be overridden before any beta route uses them.
Docker with a mounted data folder: recreating the container loses saved keys unless QA_KEYS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set.
A copy of the whole disk or home folder includes both the file and the default key.
An undecryptable file is replaced on the next save and the old keys are lost.
The no-keychain test in packages/core/tests/ai-provider.test.ts now creates key-file.key in the real user config folder, including on CI.
SECURITY.md:28 and docs/CONFIGURATION.md:69-71 still describe a plaintext file until the docs task updates them.
handoff: BE-009 calls resolveServiceKey('pagespeed') and handles null. The audit-settings route saves with saveServiceKey('pagespeed', key), validates the name against SERVICE_KEY_NAMES and never returns the key. SessionKeyResolver (beta.ts) must override the service-key methods before any beta route uses them. DOC-002 updates SECURITY.md:28, docs/CONFIGURATION.md:69-71, notes 'amended by 0034' on ADR 0002 and indexes 0034.
